faq.q: How do I convert Celsius to Fahrenheit?
faq.a: Multiply the Celsius value by 9/5 and add 32. For example, 100°C = (100 × 9/5) + 32 = 212°F.

faq.q: How do I convert Fahrenheit to Celsius?
faq.a: Subtract 32 from the Fahrenheit value and multiply by 5/9. For example, 68°F = (68 − 32) × 5/9 = 20°C.

faq.q: What is the difference between Celsius and Kelvin?
faq.a: Kelvin starts at absolute zero (−273.15°C) and uses the same step size as Celsius. To convert: K = °C + 273.15.
100°C equals 212°F, the boiling point of water at sea level.
